items.title: Manuel Mello Interview, 1959-08-03
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] What were their names? Sheik was one of them? [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah. Albert Six was the bass player. They used to call them Engelbats Sinks. Johnny Boimason, Weinmanson, he was a guitar player. Johnny Shank was a fiddle player. And Batstucker was a cornet player.

ctx.x: I heard Brad Stecker, the oldest trumpet player in the city right now. He was, uh, he used to play with, uh, I used to do a little reporting for the International Jazz. That's a year, four years back. And, uh, they used to rehearse once a week on a Wednesday night. On. With a good Betholome in there. Dolphine. And I used to go there. Well, my daddy was a pretty good friend of Shanks. And, uh, I used to go over there and listen to him. Now, I'll say this for Bat Steckler. He could do what I couldn't do. Bat…
What were their names? Sheik was one of them?

Yeah. Albert Six was the bass player. They used to call them Engelbats Sinks. Johnny Boimason, Weinmanson, he was a guitar player. Johnny Shank was a fiddle player. And Batstucker was a cornet player. Well, that's the first string band that I know of that had a blowing instrument in it. All the rest of them had a bass violin guitar man and a bass violin guitar three piece band, you know? So, he was the first one that played with a blowing horn in it. Bat was good. Bat used to be a case. Brick Lane today go play…
